rationale: Replacing TS_RANK with the current/3-year-average inventory ratio produces a multiplier tightly centered on 1.0, so the product collapses to little more than raw scaled accruals (the Sloan anomaly) with a noisy scaling wobble, making it both a cosmetic variant of the archived Historical Inventory Accrual Exposure signal and a likely rediscovery of the plain accrual effect.

The stated mechanism is inconsistent with the data definitions — Compustat `dp` is depreciation *and* amortization, so `dpc - dp` is a small reconciliation residual rather than an isolate of intangible amortization, meaning the "refinement" mostly adds noise to the archived net-intangible signal.

A substantive horizon extension of the archive's strongest signal that is naturally bounded in [-1,1], sign-consistent with the hypothesis, and motivated by a credible measurement-error argument (project timing and accrual reversals), though it remains an incremental refinement rather than a new mechanism and coverage will fall with the 3-year requirement.

Taking the absolute accrual value places large-negative-accrual (cash-rich earnings) issuers in the same adverse tail as aggressive accruers, which directly contradicts the well-documented accrual anomaly the expected negative sign relies on, so the expression fights its own hypothesis.

Because consolidating an acquired firm's balance sheet mechanically produces a large |Δwcap|, the product is largely deal size squared and thus mostly re-expresses the known acquirer-underperformance/asset-growth anomaly rather than isolating any integration-quality mechanism.

With lagged assets in the denominator the conditioning term reduces to roughly `dlc/at`, so this is a cosmetic rescaling of the already-weak archived Maturity-Pressure Accrual Growth signal (fmb -0.95, ls_talpha -1.22) with an ad hoc `|dltt| + at` denominator and no new economic content.
